Work so that an interruption loses nothing: commit and push at every checkpoint (at least once per ticket stage), open each PR as a draft as soon as its first commit exists, keep narration short, and do not rerun full suites more than this brief asks. If you are cut off, the coordinator can finish validation from your pushed branch.

MACHINE LIMITS
- 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 9 GB free disk, shared with one sibling thread (it is splitting crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs; stay out of that file and out of gmail/types.rs).
- Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target for every cargo/mise command (shared build cache; never hardcode a target dir). One heavy command at a time, including across subagents. Run `mise run install:ui` once before `mise run check:all`.
- Shared test support now exists: `mail_core::testing` behind the `test-support` feature (scripted fake provider, `until`, TempDir profiles, worker gates). Use it; do not write new ad-hoc fakes, temp directories or sleeps.

RULES FOR EVERY TICKET
- Behaviour-preserving unless a ticket says otherwise. The Gmail profile database holds a user's durable local intent (pending operations, undo records, groups, reminders, the saved split, destination snapshots). The user dogfoods Gmail mode on a real mailbox, and this VM cannot test against a real account, so migration and storage changes must be proven by tests against realistic old databases, not by inspection.
- No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement; report counts before and after (baseline: 316 mail-core, 12 email-os, 1,454 frontend).
- Update docs/current-architecture.md and docs/development.md when module boundaries or behaviour change.
- Synthetic data only. If a ticket is wrong about the code, or you find a real bug or a decision outside scope, stop and report with evidence.

THREE TICKETS, THREE PRs, IN THIS ORDER (each stacked on the previous)

TICKET 9: ordered Gmail schema migrations (PR 1)
Facts on main: crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs is 8,588 lines. `GmailStore::migrate` (from about line 174, roughly 360 lines) is one transaction of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements plus `has_column` probes for added columns and several backfills. The version marker is `meta.schema_version`; `SCHEMA_VERSION` is "gmail-2", and the check at about line 477 accepts both "gmail-1" and "gmail-2" without ever rewriting "gmail-1", so the marker carries no information and the real schema state is whatever the probes find. The same function also rewrites `gmail_operations` rows from 'applying' to 'outcome_unknown' (crash recovery that runs on every open as a side effect of migrating); there is also a separate `recover_interrupted_operations` near line 3038.
Do:
- Before changing anything, capture what current main produces: a golden of the full schema (`sqlite_master`, normalised) for a fresh database, committed as a test fixture, plus legacy databases built from the historical shapes the probes handle today (at minimum: a "gmail-1" database without the probed columns and tables, and a "gmail-2" one at each intermediate shape you can reconstruct from git history of store.rs). Populate the legacy databases with representative rows: account, threads and messages, operations in every status including 'applying', undo and group rows, a reminder, a saved split, a destination snapshot.
- Replace the probe-driven function with numbered, ordered migrations and a recorded version that always advances to the current one. Each migration runs in a transaction, is idempotent on re-entry after a crash, and a database with an unknown or newer version still fails closed exactly as today.
- Move crash recovery out of migration into an explicit startup step that runs after migration. Make clear how it relates to `recover_interrupted_operations` and collapse the two only if they are provably the same thing.
- Done when: a fresh database and every upgraded legacy database end with the same schema as the golden (state any justified difference, such as column order after ALTER), every legacy row is preserved with the same meaning (assert on the data, including that unknown legacy facts stay unknown), an interrupted migration re-runs to the same result, reopening an already-current database changes nothing, the existing migration tests (for example the triage-fact and inbox-membership backfill tests) still pass unmodified or are named as replaced, and a "gmail-1" profile ends at the current version.
- Do not change the fixture store's migrations (crates/mail-core/src/store.rs); it has its own scheme and a separate decision is pending on that backend.

TICKET 10: split gmail/store.rs by responsibility (PR 2, stacked on PR 1)
- Split into focused modules sharing the existing connection and transaction boundaries, for example: schema/migrations, cache and list queries, sync ingestion (discovery, history, eviction), operations (acceptance, claim, finish, retry), undo, groups, reminders, search, destinations. Keep `GmailStore` as the type; split its impl across files. Preserve transaction scope exactly: nothing that was atomic may become two transactions, and group acceptance and reconciliation must stay atomic.
- Move the inline #[cfg(test)] modules (about 3,300 lines, 41 tests) into adjacent test files next to the code they cover, alongside the existing *_tests.rs files.
- Make it reviewable as moves: no logic edits in the same commits as moves; say how to verify (for example `git diff --color-moved` and an unchanged public and pub(crate) surface).
- Done when: no production file in gmail/ store code exceeds roughly 1,000 lines, the crate's public API and behaviour are unchanged, and test counts are identical.

TICKET 12: stop discarding storage errors (PR 3, stacked on PR 2)
- Today about 490 call sites do `map_err(|_| MailError::StorageUnavailable)` (349 in gmail/store.rs, 127 in store.rs, a few in drafts/store.rs, store/reminders.rs and src-tauri/src/main.rs) and nothing is logged anywhere, so a storage failure cannot be diagnosed.
- Route them through one small helper per crate that records the SQLite result code and extended code plus a static call-site label, then returns the same `MailError` as today. The wire error must not change.
- Add a minimal log sink. The project promise is that no subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids or SQL with bound values are ever logged: log error codes and static labels only, never `rusqlite::Error`'s Display text if it can contain data. Decide and justify the mechanism (the `log` facade with a tiny stderr logger initialised by the shell is acceptable; adding that one dependency is in scope). Add a test that provokes a storage error containing synthetic "sensitive" text and asserts the log line contains the code and label and none of the text.
- Mutex-poison and thread-join mappings are not SQLite errors; label them distinctly rather than pretending they have a code.
- Done when: every storage failure path logs exactly one diagnosable line, the privacy test passes, and behaviour and wire errors are unchanged.

VALIDATION BEFORE EACH PR LEAVES DRAFT
- mise run check:all (core, contract, lint for both crates, frontend, typecheck, native tests, web build). Report exact counts.
- For PR 1 and PR 2 also run `cargo test --locked -p mail-core` five times in a row with two CPU hogs running (for example two `yes > /dev/null`, killed afterwards) and report the loop output; the suite was made deterministic last phase and must stay that way.
- CI runs check:all on every PR targeting main; stacked PRs that target another branch do not get CI until retargeted, so say which head you validated locally.

DELIVERY
- Three PRs with gh (`-R BbrSofiane/email-os`; the git remote is a proxy URL): PR 1 against main; PR 2 and PR 3 stacked, each noting what it depends on. Do not merge. The coordinator merges PR 1 as soon as it is green, then asks you to retarget.

I validated #48 and #49 locally on those heads.

## Ticket 9 (#46)
- **Migrations:** `meta.schema_version` now advances through `gmail-migrations-1` to `-9`. Each stage is one transaction and re-runs safely after a crash. A profile already at the current version writes nothing, and an unknown or newer version still fails closed.
- **Recovery:** crash recovery runs as an explicit startup step after migration. I did not merge it with `recover_interrupted_operations`: startup recovery is global and leaves `failure` alone, while the reconnect-time one is account-scoped and also clears `failure`.
- **Legacy shapes covered:** gmail-1, the gmail-2 operations profile, and gmail-3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16. Each is seeded with synthetic rows, migrated, and checked: rows kept, unknown facts still unknown, saved split, reminder, snapshot and reply context still readable, `applying` ending as `outcome_unknown`, schema equal to the golden.
- **Schema difference from the golden:** in gmail-9 to gmail-12, `is_starred` keeps its old `CHECK (is_starred IN (0,1))`. SQLite can't drop a CHECK with `ALTER TABLE`, and main never rebuilt the table either, so the test allows this for those four shapes only.
- **Tests changed:**
  - Three tests faked a legacy profile by dropping a column but kept the current version marker. They now also set the legacy `gmail-2` marker, because the probes that used to repair them on every open are gone. Assertions are unchanged and none was deleted. These are two in `gmail/store.rs` and `stars::legacy_migration_keeps_unknown_stars_and_query_scope_fails_closed`.
  - The triage-fact and inbox-membership backfill tests pass unchanged.

## Ticket 10 (#48)
- `store.rs` went from 8,297 lines to 215, and the largest of 18 new modules is 687 lines.
- The change is two move-only commits, with docs updated. Function bodies are unchanged. The only edits are `fn` becoming `pub(super)`, plus three private methods widened to `pub(super)`. `GmailStore` has 67 `pub`/`pub(crate)` methods before and after, and each method still opens the same single transaction, so group acceptance and reconciliation stay atomic.
- I did not split the tests by responsibility. The 3,276-line inline test module is now one file, `store_tests.rs`, next to `migration_tests.rs`. Splitting it further is possible if you want it.
- To verify, run `git diff --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change` on each commit.

## Ticket 12 (#49)
- **Routing:** about 510 `map_err` sites and 48 direct `StorageUnavailable` constructions now log one line and return the same `MailError::StorageUnavailable`. The shell's 16 sites are lock-poison, task-join and path errors, so they get distinct cause tags (`lock_poisoned`, `thread_join`, `path_unavailable`) instead of a code.
- **Mechanism:** the `log` facade (already in `Cargo.lock`; the diff is just two dependency edges) plus a stderr logger the shell installs. The logger only passes the two storage targets.
- **What a line contains:** `file:line` via `#[track_caller]`, a static cause tag and the numeric SQLite codes. The error's Display text is never read.
- **Privacy tests:** they provoke real SQLite errors whose own text quotes a synthetic subject, address and column name. Each test first confirms the raw error contains that text, then asserts the log line has the code and site and none of the text.
- **Not logged:** rejections because the sync service is stopped or halted. The failure that halted it was already logged, so logging every rejected call would be noise.

- `cargo test --locked -p mail-core` ran five times in a row with two CPU hogs on #46 and on #48. All 10 runs passed, and the hogs were killed afterwards.
- Not run: rendered tests, native smoke, the Gmail-upgrade gate, or anything against a real account. Those are yours.
